title: IT Act s. 10A — Validity of contracts formed through electronic means (IT Act s. 10A)

content.overview: Validity of contracts formed through electronic means. content.study:
Core rule
Section 10A provides that a contract is not unenforceable merely because proposals, acceptance or revocation are expressed or communicated electronically, subject to the Act and other applicable law.

Textual analysis
Identify each operative definition, condition, exception and legal consequence. Do not replace a statutory definition with ordinary usage.

Application
Map the facts to each element and identify the relevant electronic record, system, contract, signature, data or security control. Separate technical facts from the legal proposition they support.

Evidence
Where electronic records are relied upon, apply BSA 2023 s. 63 where applicable and separately analyse authenticity, integrity, attribution and weight.

Boundaries
Distinguish this topic from neighbouring IT Act provisions, contractual remedies, privacy rights and regulatory duties. A shared factual event does not make all provisions interchangeable.

Current-law caution
Use the statutory text and applicable rules in force on the relevant date; do not treat struck-down section 66A as current law.

cases.name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court reviewed restrictions on online speech under the Information Technology Act.
cases.issue: Whether IT Act s. 66A impermissibly restricted constitutional speech.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 66A was vague and overbroad and violated Article 19(1)(a); it was not saved by Article 19(2).
cases.holding: Section 66A was struck down in its entirety.
cases.relevance: Use only as historical status; do not present s. 66A as a current offence.

cases.name: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer
cases.facts: The Court examined the statutory method for proving electronic records.
cases.issue: Whether electronic records can be admitted without the applicable certificate route.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Electronic records must satisfy the special statutory proof requirements applicable to computer outputs.
cases.holding: The Court reaffirmed the certificate discipline for electronic evidence.
cases.relevance: Use with BSA s. 63 and digital-record admissibility.

cases.name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Constitution Bench considered privacy as a constitutional right in the digital and modern State.
cases.issue: Whether privacy is protected as a Fundamental Right.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Privacy is intrinsic to dignity, liberty and Part III, subject to legality, legitimate aim, proportionality and procedural safeguards.
cases.relevance: Use for surveillance, data protection and informational privacy.

I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether IT Act s. 10A — Validity of contracts formed through electronic means (IT Act s. 10A) applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
IT Act s. 10A — Validity of contracts formed through electronic means (IT Act s. 10A) is governed by Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles. identify the date, technology, applicable IT Act provision, data regime, intermediary rule and evidence law; distinguish struck-down provisions from current offences.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.
